items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: he used to give me strings whenever he'd see me

ctx.x: Were you taught music in any formal way by music teachers in school or anyplace else?

No. I had some -- there was a bass player named Truck Parham - saw me out on the street, you know, with my fiddle, he said, "Come by the house" -- and I went by his house one day; you know, I didn't have no money to pay him but he wanted to help me -- a young kid, you know -- and he showed me how he played double stops. Then there was another bassist out there, Henry Ford, and Taupus Dean, and a bassist named Walter Williams. I don't know what ever happened to him -- he used to give me strings whenever he'd see…

Because I remember Erskine Tate was working down at one of those dance marathons -- what was the name of that club down on Wabash -- we'd stop by there and try to play; kind of spare the musicians a little bit -- a lot of people was dancing for these prizes. You know what I mean by a dance marathon? Dance for weeks.
